payload.title: Filtering through queries
payload.summary: This Jupyter notebook demonstrates the use of the PyLiPD Python package to filter LiPD formatted datasets. It focuses on filtering datasets by archive types, geographic location, time intervals, variable names, proxies, and resolution. The notebook uses the Euro2k database as an example dataset and illustrates how to manipulate LiPD objects and convert them into LiPDSeries objects for more granular filtering. The outputs include filtered datasets and merged dataframes containing essential time series information.
goals: Use existing APIs to filter datasets according to archive types, location, and variable names.
Understand the concept of a LiPDSeries object and how it differs from a LiPD object.

section_blurbs.blurb: Introduces the PyLiPD package and its capabilities for filtering LiPD datasets using predefined APIs.
section_blurbs.heading: Filtering through queries

section_blurbs.blurb: Demonstrates filtering datasets using geographic bounding boxes and combining filters for archive types.
section_blurbs.heading: Filtering by location

section_blurbs.blurb: Explains how to filter datasets based on specific time intervals and record lengths.
section_blurbs.heading: Filtering by time interval

section_blurbs.blurb: Describes converting LiPD objects to LiPDSeries objects for filtering by variable names and merging dataframes.
section_blurbs.heading: Filtering on the `LiPDSeries` object

section_blurbs.blurb: Shows how to filter datasets based on standardized proxy fields in LiPD files.
section_blurbs.heading: Filtering by proxy

section_blurbs.blurb: Illustrates filtering datasets by resolution metrics such as mean and median.
section_blurbs.heading: Filtering by resolution

outputs: Merged dataframes with time series information
